title: Flexible Reservation Windows and Fairness Heuristics for Dedicated Tenancy
creator: Ava Mitra
overview: Introduce flexible reservation windows and tenant fairness heuristics to improve utilization of Dedicated pools while protecting committed throughput SLAs. The feature allows tenants to book reserved capacity with configurable window granularity (hourly/daily/rolling), opt into queued burst fallback behavior, and apply fairness policies that influence preemption and burst allocation under contention.
problem_statement: Current reserved pools are rigid: reservations are fixed to calendar slots and lack configurable grace/burst behavior. This leads to underutilized GPU capacity during short-term usage spikes and causes noisy-neighbor effects when multiple tenants attempt bursts simultaneously. Operators lack fine-grained controls to balance committed SLA guarantees against short-term efficient utilization.
goals: Allow tenants to reserve capacity in flexible rolling windows with configurable granularity (1h, 6h, 24h)
Expose a tenant-facing toggle for controlled burst allowance with three modes (None, Soft, Managed) and corresponding billing semantics
Implement a fairness heuristic in the scheduler that weights reservations, recent usage, and tenant priority to decide burst grants under contention
Provide console UX and API to create/modify reservations and preview expected availability and cost impact
Ship telemetry and alerting for reservation utilization, preemption events, and fairness violations
non_goals: Rewriting the entire autoscaler or replacing existing reserved pool admission logic
Supporting per-request custom kernels or hardware selection (out of scope for this ticket)
Automated cross-region spillover routing for bursts (future work)
success_metrics: Increase average Dedicated pool GPU utilization during working hours by >= 8% within 6 weeks of rollout
Reduce customer-reported burst failures due to contention by 60% for tenants who opt into Managed burst mode
No regression in committed SLA latency (p95) for reserved tenants after rollout
Console NPS for reservation UX >= +30 in rollout cohort surveys
user_stories: As a platform engineer, I want to create a rolling 6-hour reservation so my workload has predictable capacity for intermittent peak periods
As an SRE, I want a fairness dashboard to audit which tenants are being preempted or denied burst capacity
As an account owner, I want to opt my reserved pool into Soft burst mode so it can accept short bursts when unused without risking SLA violations
As a billing admin, I want clear usage telemetry showing how burst credits were consumed and any overage charges
requirements: API: POST /dedicated/reservations with fields: tenant_id, pool_id, start_ts, end_ts, granularity, burst_mode, priority_tier
API: PATCH /dedicated/reservations to adjust rolling windows and burst_mode
Console: reservation creation flow with capacity preview, utilization heatmap, and estimated monthly cost delta
Scheduler: implement fairness scoring function that combines reservation weight, recent token consumption, and explicit tenant priority; output must be deterministic and explainable
Scheduler: support preemption window with safe-evict flag to gracefully terminate non-reserved workloads within X seconds and preserve KV cache where feasible
Telemetry: emit events for reservation_create, reservation_update, burst_granted, burst_denied, preemption_triggered with tenant_id and reservation_id
Billing: tag burst usage with burst_mode to apply correct pricing (free buffer for Soft, premium for Managed bursts)
Governance: RBAC checks for reservation APIs tied to account roles and enterprise entitlements
Docs: PRD and public support article describing modes, billing, and recommended patterns
Testing: end-to-end tests that simulate three tenants contending for a single pool under overlapping reservations
acceptance_criteria: A tenant can create a rolling reservation via API and see it reflected in the console within 10s
Scheduler assigns burst capacity according to the configured mode and fairness heuristic in simulation tests with reproducible outcomes
Preemption sequence completes within the configured grace window and emits telemetry events capture the sequence
Feature flags allow gradual rollout (beta cohort by workspace tag) and can be toggled without redeploying runtime
Billing tags are applied correctly in usage export and cost estimates shown in console match exported billing within 1% on test data
Manual QA verifies console heatmap and capacity preview show anticipated availability for three different reservation granularities
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Beta, 2 weeks): Feature flag enabled for 5 pilot customers. Monitor telemetry and SLA signals closely.
Phase 2 (Gradual, 4 weeks): Open to workspaces with dedicated pools under 50% utilization. Collect UX feedback and fix console bugs.
Phase 3 (General): Enable for all dedicated customers and update billing documentation and support playbooks
Safety net: automatic rollback if p95 latency for reserved workloads increases by >15% or if burst_denied events spike beyond threshold
risks: Incorrect fairness scoring could unintentionally starve smaller tenants—mitigate by simulation tests and throttled rollout
Telemetry gaps may delay detection of regressions; add high-cardinality alerting during beta
Billing mismatch edge cases for mixed-mode pools (Soft + Managed) require careful rounding rules
Preemption may impact long-running KV-cache-heavy requests; need safe-evict design and validation
notes: Next steps: schedule cross-functional review with Eng (runtime/scheduler), Billing, and Support. Create a small simulation harness to validate fairness scores against historical tenant traces. Confirm SLA testbench metrics with Reliability team before Beta launch.
